category_title: Collaborative students who adopt a teaching role to support their own learning
minimal_context: Jenna is working on an independent reading session using the Achieve 3000 program and is prompted to type a summary in the text box.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent reading. Please read the article on the Achieve 3000 program and type your response in the summary strategy text box.

STUDENT: I was just helping the new student learn to navigate through the reading program. Can I keep talking her through it instead?

TUTOR: You need to work independently right now. Please start your summary.

STUDENT: But I already understand the story from our discussion earlier. I even showed my partner how to enlarge the text so we could read it better.

TUTOR: That is fine, but you still need to use the summary strategy provided by the program.

STUDENT: I don't want to use the summary strategy. It is just too difficult and time consuming to type my responses into the text box.

options.A: Provide a ticket for each behavioral expectation met, which can be exchanged for a break or classroom reward.
options.B: Pair the student with a new classmate during the study period to help them navigate the reading program.
options.C: Have the student use a digital note-taking tool to organize their work and archive past reading summaries.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete their typed summaries during the independent reading session.
